results.title: Lymphedema - Medical Clinical Policy Bulletins
results.content: Aetna considers home use of a segmented pneumatic compression device with manual control of the pressure in each chamber medically necessary for the treatment of lymphedema extending onto the chest, trunk and/or abdomen when all of the following are met: (Sleeves and gloves are separate items; as such, if both should be required for treatment, three gloves and three sleeves per affected arm would be considered medically necessary initially, with two additional of each in subsequent 6 month intervals, if needed.)  For members whose plans exclude coverage of supplies, static compression sleeves are only covered for intractable lymphedema of the arms due to mastectomy for breast cancer.Footnote1\* 9. Combined intermittent pneumatic compression and complete decongestive therapy for the treatment of breast cancer-related upper limb lymphedema The efficacy of intermittent pneumatic compression as a substitute for manual lymphatic drainage in complete decongestive therapy in the treatment of breast cancer related lymphedema. Manual lymph drainage combined with compression therapy for arm lymphedema following breast cancer treatment (Alert).
